Each occurrence of this entity represents a single organisation. An organisation is said to come into existence when it is incorporated or when another entity chooses to recognise it for some purpose. It will no longer exist if it is dissolved or if no other entities choose to recognise it.

There need only be one occurrence of this entity for each organisation no matter how many other entities reference it over time.

An organisation usually has a type that defines its function or purpose.

It is not uncommon for there to be formal relationships between organisations. A common example is a global organisation which is comprised of multiple subsidiaries. We may refer to the regional organisations as sections or divisions. However, for the sake of this module, we define each entity independently. Other modules will address the structural relationship between different organisations.
The moment the organisation was incorporated. Optional if there is an incorporation event; otherwise, it is mandatory.
The moment the organisation was recognised for informational purposes. Optional if there is an incorporation event; otherwise, it is mandatory.
The moment the organisations characteristics took on the specified values.
The moment the organisations's recognition was revoked for informational purposes. Optional if there is an dissolution event; otherwise, it is mandatory.
The moment the organisation was disolved.
The moment the organisations's details were deleted. An occurrence of this event will cause all other events for the organization to be disregarded.
The number of organisations at the moment the reporting period opened. This count is carried forward from the previous reporting period and is equal to the closing count for that period.
The number of organisations incorporated or recognised the moment the reporting period started. These organisations are not included in the opening count but are included in the starting count.
The number of organisations at the moment the reporting period started.
The number of organisations incorporated or recognised during the reporting period but after the moment the reporting period started.
The total number of organisations incorporated or recognised during the reporting period.

A count of the number of organisations during the reporting period. In most cases, each organisation will be counted once; however, if it were derecognised and then recognised again within the period, it would be counted twice.

A weighted count of the number of organisations during the reporting period. If an organisation is active for the entire period, it will be counted as 1; if it is active for half the period, it will be counted as 0.5.
The total number of organisations dissolved or derecognised during the reporting period.
The number of organisations dissolved or derecognised during the reporting period but before the moment the reporting period ended.
The number of organisations at the moment the reporting period ended.
The number of organisations dissolved or derecognised the moment the reporting period ended. These organisations are not included in the closing count but are included in the ending count.
The number of organisations at the moment the reporting period closed. This count is carried forward to the next reporting period and is equal to the opening count for that period.

The size of the population carried forward from the previous reporting period.
The number of people that joined the population at the moment the reporting period started. These people are not included in the opening count, but are included in the starting count.
The size of the population at the moment the reporting period started.

Each occurrence of this entity represents a single person. A person is said to come into existence when they are born or when another entity chooses to recognise them for some purpose. They will no longer exist if they are deceased or if no entities choose to recognise them. A person may participate in different roles (e.g. acquaintance, colleague, contact, contractor, employee, relation...) at different times. There need only be one occurrence of this entity for each person, no matter how many roles they play across time.

Each occurrence of this entity represents a single person. A person is said to come into existence when they are born or when we chooses to recognise them for informational purposes. They will no longer exist if they are deceased or if we choose not to recognise them. A person may participate in different roles (e.g. acquaintance, colleague, contact, contractor, employee, relation...) at different times. There need only be one occurrence of this entity for each person, no matter how many roles they play across time.
The unique identifier assigned to the person.
The effective moment of the event. See the events for an explanation of how the effective moment is interpreted for each event.
The sequence of the event within the moment. If multiple events occur at the same moment, then we can use this data item to define the sequence.
The event identifier. See the events for a list of acceptable identifiers.
The person's personal or national identifier.
The person's family names.
The person's given names.
The moment the person was born.
The moment the person was recognised for informational purposes.
The moment associated characteristics took on the specified values. The moment from which the modification applied.
The moment the person's recognition was revoked for informational purposes. The moment from which the person was no longer recognised.
The moment the person died. The moment from which the person was no longer alive.
The moment the person's details were deleted. The moment from which the person entity was deleted.
The number of people present at the opening moment of a reporting period.
The number of people recognised at the first moment of a reporting period.
The number of people present at the start of a reporting period.
The number of people recognised during a reporting period.
The number of people present at any moment within the reporting period.
The weighted number of people present within a reporting period.
The number of people derecognised during a reporting period.
The number of people present at the end of a reporting period.
The number of people derecognised at the last moment of a reporting period.
The number of people present at the closing moment of a reporting period.

Each occurrence of this entity represents a language spoken by a person. It is possible for a person to speak multiple languages, acquire a new language, and even loose the ability to speak a language.
